concept.name: Gravestone doji
concept.definition: A doji variant in which the open, low, and close are equal or nearly equal, leaving a long upper shadow and little or no lower shadow (an inverted T). Technical analysts read it as intraperiod buying that was fully rejected by sellers, and treat it as a possible bearish reversal sign when it appears after an advance; it is an interpretive framework, not a validated predictor.
concept.intuition: Buyers drove price sharply higher during the period, but sellers forced it all the way back down to the opening level, showing supply sitting above the market.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: open, low, and close cluster at or near the same price (small tolerance), while the high sits far above, so the upper shadow dominates the range. It is the single-candle mirror of the dragonfly doji.
concept.failure_modes: In strong uptrends the rejection is often temporary profit-taking and the trend resumes, so reversal readings fail. It is also common and meaningless in flat, low-volume sessions.
concept.misconceptions: A gravestone doji is not automatically a sell signal; after a decline it can instead mark seller exhaustion. It needs bearish confirmation from the next candle.
concept.example: After a rally, a stock opens at 60.00, spikes to 63.00, and is sold back down to close at 60.00. The gravestone doji shows the highs were rejected; traders look for a lower close the following session before acting on a bearish reading.
